newsitem.title: UK: Romania to get World Bank loans next week - minister.
newsitem.headline: Romania to get World Bank loans next week - minister.

text.p: The World Bank is expected to approve about $600 million in credits for Romania next week, Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara said on Thursday.
"(Next) Tuesday the World Bank will approve (the agreed) loans for agriculture, restructuring and social protection," Ciumara told a news conference in London.
Earlier this month the World Bank agreed to support Romania's shock-therapy programme launched earlier this year by the new centrist-coalition government, which ousted leftists in 1996 elections.

The Bank pledged to lend Romania some $625 million this year. The credits followed a standby loan from the International Monetary Fund of $430 million approved last month to back up Romania's reforms.
Speaking at a presentation for investors ahead of the launch of the country's first mark-denominated Eurobond, Ciumara also said IMF officials would visit Bucharest next week.
Ciumara said Poul Thomsen, IMF chief negotiator for Romania, would come to Bucharest on Monday to review the country's reform progress.
Under radical reform steps over the past months Romania tightened monetary policies, liberalised fuel, energy and food prices and adopted an austerity budget.

It also promised to go further with privatisation and restructuring of inefficient industries and farms and slash its current account deficit to $1.4 billion this year from an estimated $2.3 billion in 1996.
Both the IMF and World Bank suspended credits for Romania last year after complaining that the leftist government then in power had overshot spending targets.
